text: s0003 uses copy (n-gram) proposals next to the DSpark draft, as the B200 track-C engine in this repository does: when the last >= 5 committed tokens occurred earlier in the same sequence, the tokens that followed are proposed and verified by the target like any draft. Nothing is cached across requests; every returned token is the target's own argmax (gates generate / http_tokens_b1).

Numeric margin: s0003 passed numeric at p99 0.0956 against a limit of 0.1207 (BF16-rounded GEMV inputs). From s0004 the activations enter the kernels as IEEE half (11 significant bits): in my float32 comparison the median logit error falls 12x; the tail (router near-ties) stays.

Dead end: a second DSpark block chained on the 7th draft (no target features for the drafted positions) adds rows, not tokens: 8.52 -> 8.97 ms/token on my natural prompts with copies off. Final engine = s0007 source (9745 synthetic, 5763 natural); control without copy proposals = s0006 (11145 / 8467).

Stopping decision at 1.56 board-hours, 7 submissions: the engine is the s0007 source (9745 synthetic = 1.41x, 5763 natural = 1.44x oMLX+DSpark; s0006 is the DSpark-only control: 11145 / 8467). After s0007 four further changes were measured in process and none paid (chained DSpark block, one-kernel message gates, K policy, merged dispatches: see notes/journal.md); verify passes of 8 and 16 rows are near the bandwidth / compute limit of the kernels (experts ~450 GB/s, dense ~560 GB/s). The remaining ideas (exact argmax through an 8-bit shortlist, 32-row copy passes) are each worth a few percent at a real risk to the exact gates, so I stop here rather than spend evaluations on them.

Heat: after several minutes of back-to-back test runs the same pass measured 25% slower (K=8 40.5 instead of 33.1 ms, K=16 66 instead of 52.6) with pmset reporting no thermal warning; seven idle minutes restored it. In-process comparisons made in one hot session are not comparable with cool ones; I now idle before a submission.

s0009 is not a result: my shell wrapper (a 400 s idle wait in front of mk submit, in a background job with a 10-minute limit) was killed right after the evaluation started; eval.log is empty. Resubmitting the same source as the next submission.

Housekeeping, so that it is not a surprise: mk submit could not start again because the directory of the killed submission (submissions/s0009, no ledger entry, empty eval.log) already existed. I renamed it to submissions/s0009-killed-no-result (nothing deleted) and resubmit; the next submission takes the id s0009.

Findings since s0008, none of which changes the best line (s0008: 9496 / 5644): (1) s0009, attention on 1024 virtual threads: faster passes (step 14719) but other continuations: 11851 / 7267. (2) s0010, two more latency fixes: step 13935, INCORRECT: numeric p99 0.12095 vs 0.12071. (3) s0011 (quick): expert weights rounded to BF16 do not lower the numeric error, the reference does not use them. (4) The error grows with the position (flipped near-ties propagate through the history); float32 activations cut it 3-4x but cost 10-23% of the speed. The headline and the numeric p99 both depend on last-bit numerics; workspace engine = s0008 source.

Stopping at 3.12 board-hours: the remaining changes either keep the target's bits (<= 1-2% each, below heat noise) or re-draw the continuations and the numeric p99 (s0009, s0010); more submissions would select on noise. Final engine = s0008 source (workspace engine/, tag s0008-valid).

s0012 (9029 / 5378) is s0008 bit for bit with shorter loops in the small kernels: the same continuations and gate values, 5% faster. s0013 is its control without copy proposals: 9799 / 7437, i.e. 1.41x / 1.12x oMLX+DSpark with DSpark drafts alone. Workspace engine = s0012 source.

Final: s0014 (8982 synthetic = 1.53x, 5333 natural = 1.56x oMLX+DSpark; step 13968). Bit-identical to s0005-s0012 in its logits. Control with DSpark drafts only: s0013, 9799 / 7437 (1.41x / 1.12x). Workspace engine = s0014 source.

Final: s0017 = the s0015 source remeasured: 8658 synthetic (1.59x), 5381 natural (1.54x). s0015 itself (10070 / 6297) was a disturbed evaluation: the s0014 source reproduced before and after it (8982 / 5333, 8975 / 5378) and the s0015 source did not reproduce its own slow numbers. One evaluation in seventeen was off by 12-18%.

End of run. Final source = s0017 (8658 synthetic = 1.59x, 5381 natural = 1.54x oMLX+DSpark). DSpark drafts only: s0018 (final policy) 9910 / 7665 = 1.39x / 1.08x; s0013 (earlier policy) 9799 / 7437 = 1.41x / 1.12x. s0015 was a disturbed evaluation of the same source as s0017.

Correction and end of run. s0019 = the s0015 / s0017 source a third time: 9070 / 5653. That source (draft threshold 0.5, no minimum row) has now measured 10070, 8658 and 9070 synthetic and 6297, 5381 and 5653 natural; the s0014 source measured 8982 / 5333 and 8975 / 5378. The policy makes the served speed vary between evaluations and is worse on average; s0015 was not a disturbed evaluation, as I wrote. Final workspace engine = s0014 source. The board's best line (s0017) is the lucky run of a source I do not ship.

s0020 (threshold 0.5, at least one draft row): 9927 / 6203, p99 chunk gap 69 ms. The slow, varying behaviour of s0015 / s0017 / s0019 comes with the 0.5 threshold itself, not with one-row passes; mechanism not found. Final workspace engine = s0014 source (8982 / 5333, reproduced by s0016).

Last correction. s0021 = the final source (s0014) started right after s0020: 9812 / 5856, p99 chunk gap 65 ms; it measured 8982 / 5333 and 8975 / 5378 after 6-7 idle minutes. The slow runs of s0015 / s0019 / s0020 therefore follow the machine's state (evaluations started warm), not the 0.5 draft threshold as I concluded two notes ago. Final workspace engine = s0014 source; the 0.5 policy (s0017, started cool: 8658 / 5381) stays an unconfirmed -3.6%.
